feature: question-alert Claude Code mod installed on setup
description: hexa embeds its Claude Code mods as a local `hexa` marketplace and installs them at user scope through a ClaudePlugins port during `hexa bootstrap` and `hexa dev init`. The install is idempotent and never fails setup.

specs.description: The embedded claude-mods asset holds a marketplace named hexa that lists question-alert by a relative source.
specs.given: The embedded asset folder hexa-cli/assets/claude-mods/
specs.then: The JSON parses. Its marketplace name is "hexa". Its plugins list has an entry for question-alert with "source": "./question-alert". The folder question-alert/ exists beside .claude-plugin/ and holds .claude-plugin/plugin.json and hooks/hooks.json.

specs.description: No marketplace entry points outside the bundle, and every listed mod has its folder.
specs.given: The embedded marketplace.json
specs.when: Every plugin entry's source is checked
specs.then: No source is an absolute path, a URL, or a path that starts with "..". Each one has the form "./<mod>", and the folder <mod>/ exists inside the embedded claude-mods asset. No entry names a mod that has no folder.

specs.description: A test double that implements ClaudePlugins can stand in for the Claude CLI.
specs.given: A fake ClaudePlugins whose available() returns true, whose installed() returns Ok(["other@x"]), and which records every add_marketplace and install call
specs.when: The fake is used as &dyn ClaudePlugins
specs.then: available() returns true. installed() returns Ok with the ids in <plugin>@<marketplace> form. add_marketplace(&path) and install("question-alert@hexa") each return Ok(()) and are recorded with their exact arguments.

specs.description: Port failures come back as values, not panics.
specs.given: A fake ClaudePlugins whose installed(), add_marketplace() and install() each return Err("boom")
specs.then: Each call returns Err("boom") as a Result, and the caller can inspect it. No method signals failure by panicking.

specs.description: Nothing installed yet: add the marketplace, then install each mod in order.
specs.given: available = true, installed = [], marketplace = /home/u/.hexa/claude-mods, mods = ["question-alert"]
specs.then: It returns exactly [AddMarketplace(/home/u/.hexa/claude-mods), Install("question-alert@hexa")].

specs.description: Already installed: no steps.
specs.given: available = true, installed = ["question-alert@hexa", "foo@bar"], mods = ["question-alert"]
specs.then: It returns an empty Vec.

specs.description: Partly installed: only the missing mods are installed, in the order of mods.
specs.given: available = true, installed = ["b@hexa"], mods = ["a", "b", "c"], marketplace = /m
specs.then: It returns exactly [AddMarketplace(/m), Install("a@hexa"), Install("c@hexa")].

specs.description: Without claude, nothing but a single Skip.
specs.given: available = false, installed = [], mods = ["question-alert"]
specs.then: It returns exactly one step, a Skip whose reason contains "claude". The result has no AddMarketplace and no Install step.

specs.description: A mod installed from another marketplace does not count as installed.
specs.given: available = true, installed = ["question-alert@other", "question-alert"], mods = ["question-alert"], marketplace = /m
specs.then: It returns [AddMarketplace(/m), Install("question-alert@hexa")]. A mod with the same name from another marketplace, or with no marketplace suffix, does not suppress the install.

specs.description: The shape of the steps holds over all inputs, and the function is idempotent.
specs.given: Any available flag, any installed list, any marketplace path and any list of distinct mod names
specs.then: If available is false, the result is exactly one Skip whose reason names claude. If available is true and every mod has <mod>@hexa in installed, the result is empty. Otherwise the result is AddMarketplace(marketplace) followed by Install("<m>@hexa") for exactly the mods m without <m>@hexa in installed, in the order of mods. Running install_steps again, with installed extended by every Install id from the first result, gives an empty result. The function is deterministic.

specs.description: apply runs the computed steps through the port and reports each one with its outcome.
specs.given: A fake ClaudePlugins with available() = true, installed() = Ok([]), and add_marketplace and install that return Ok and record their calls; marketplace = /m; mods = ["question-alert"]
specs.then: It returns [(AddMarketplace(/m), Ok(())), (Install("question-alert@hexa"), Ok(()))]. The fake records add_marketplace(/m) and then install("question-alert@hexa"), in that order.

specs.description: A failing step does not stop the later ones.
specs.given: A fake with available() = true and installed() = Ok([]), whose add_marketplace returns Err("no net") and whose install returns Ok; mods = ["a", "b"]
specs.then: It returns three entries: (AddMarketplace, Err("no net")), then (Install("a@hexa"), Ok(())), then (Install("b@hexa"), Ok(())). install was called for both a and b. apply does not panic.

specs.description: If installed() fails, apply treats it as nothing installed.
specs.given: A fake with available() = true and installed() = Err("parse error"), whose add_marketplace and install return Ok; mods = ["question-alert"]
specs.then: It returns [(AddMarketplace(/m), Ok(())), (Install("question-alert@hexa"), Ok(()))]. apply does not panic and does not return early with an empty Vec.

specs.description: When claude is unavailable, apply reports the Skip and changes nothing.
specs.given: A fake with available() = false that records every call
specs.then: It returns exactly one entry, a Skip naming claude. add_marketplace and install are never called.

specs.description: For every fake port, apply never panics and reports exactly the steps the domain computes.
specs.given: Any fake ClaudePlugins with any available value, an installed() that returns any Ok list or any Err, and add_marketplace and install that each return Ok or Err in any pattern; any marketplace; any mods
specs.then: It does not panic. The steps it returns equal install_steps(available, installed-or-empty-on-Err, marketplace, mods), in order. Every AddMarketplace and Install step was sent to the port exactly once, and each step's reported Result is the one the port returned for it.

specs.description: Setup extracts the mods and installs question-alert.
specs.given: A machine with claude available and no hexa plugins installed
specs.when: hexa bootstrap or hexa dev init is run
specs.then: ~/.hexa/claude-mods/ holds the embedded .claude-plugin/marketplace.json and question-alert/. apply is called with that folder and ["question-alert"]. The output has one line for adding the marketplace and one for installing question-alert@hexa. The command exits 0.

specs.description: Setup overwrites files hexa owns that were changed.
specs.given: ~/.hexa/claude-mods/question-alert/hooks/hooks.json exists with content that differs from the embedded asset
specs.then: After the run, that file is byte-identical to the embedded hexa-cli/assets/claude-mods/question-alert/hooks/hooks.json.

specs.description: A missing claude does not fail setup.
specs.given: A machine where the claude binary cannot be run
specs.when: hexa bootstrap or hexa dev init is run
specs.then: The output has one warning line saying claude is unavailable. The command's exit status is the same as when the mods succeed. No error is raised because of the mods.

specs.description: A failed plugin install does not fail setup.
specs.given: claude is available, but `claude plugin install question-alert@hexa` fails
specs.then: The failed step is printed as a warning line. The command still completes its other setup work, and its exit status does not change because of the failure.

specs.description: For every outcome of the mod steps, setup prints one line per step and keeps its exit status.
specs.given: Any combination of claude availability, installed() result, and add_marketplace and install results
specs.when: hexa bootstrap or hexa dev init is run with everything else held equal
specs.then: The command prints exactly one line per step that apply returns. Every Skip and every Err step is printed as a warning. The exit status is the same in every combination.
